newsitem.title: UK: Britain pledges "no evacuation" of Montserrat.
newsitem.headline: Britain pledges "no evacuation" of Montserrat.

text.p: Britain pledged on Friday it would not evacuate the Caribbean island of Montserrat, devastated by a series of volcanic eruptions.
"I wish to make it clear that the British government have no intention of evacuating Montserrat in the present circumstances," said foreign office minister Liz Symons.

She said the government would discuss "a whole range of issues" when Chief Minister Bertrand Osborne visited London next month. Media reports had recently suggested Britain was considering evacuating the island.

"We are committed to helping the people of Montserrat by providing emergency aid now, and through a long-term programme which will maintain the economic and social viability of the island in the future," Symons said in a statement.
Volcanic eruptions on the British territory have killed about 20 people. Hundreds have fled their homes in the south of the island, which is now totally evacuated.
The island's population has dwindled to around 5,800 from about 11,000 when the Soufriere volcano roared to life in July 1995.
Earlier this month Britain said it might offer people on Montserrat an assisted package to Britain or other parts of the Caribbean plus a resettlement grant if they decided to quit their homeland.
